statements.text: It is important that Congress and regulators understand technology and create an environment that allows for innovation to flourish while also having clear rules for the road. [...] As we develop new technologies, we need to ensure that workers and the environment are protected, additional costs are put on workers struggling under rising prices, and that we create jobs and vibrant livelihoods for the middle class. I am eager to work with workers, labor, and industry to build the most innovative economy on Earth that delivers for working families.
statements.venue: Campaign website position on Artificial Intelligence (via localcandidates.org)

statements.text: The technologies that will shape the balance of global power are being built today — and Congress needs to best position America as the leader. Our adversaries are exploiting American innovation to fuel their rise and erode our strategic edge. [...] I’m proud to lead this commonsense package to give the United States the tools needed to stay ahead, secure our supply chains, and protect the technologies that power our economy and our national defense.
statements.venue: Press release on AI Sovereignty Act / tech security package

statements.text: I'm grateful for all that Professor Anand Rao has done to launch the Center for AI and the Liberal Arts at the University of Mary Washington.     As AI becomes more integrated into daily life, this center will be a key resource for UMW students.   It was a privilege to highlight Professor Rao as my Constituent of the Week.

Virginia should welcome innovation, but not at any cost. We need to ensure data centers pay their fair share and are built in places that make sense — not next to neighborhoods, schools, or our public lands. This study will help Congress make smarter decisions that protect Virginia families while supporting economic growth.
statements.venue: Press release on Smart Data Center Policy Act

statements.text: It is past time we make data centers pay their fair share. Across Virginia, families and businesses are being forced to foot the bill for massive infrastructure investments needed to power large data centers. Everywhere I go, I hear from families who cannot afford their rising monthly utility bills and Republican-led data center tax breaks aren’t going to bring those monthly costs down.
statements.venue: Press release on Reverse Big Ugly Tax Breaks for Data Centers Act

statements.text: Families in Virginia and across the country should not have to pay higher electricity bills to subsidize some of the largest and most energy-intensive data centers and computing facilities in the world. As data centers and artificial intelligence drive growing demand for electricity, we need to make sure the companies benefiting from that growth pay their fair share. My bill puts ratepayers first and protects hardworking Virginians from being stuck with higher utility bills to subsidize billion-dollar corporations.
statements.venue: Press release on Make Data Centers Pay Act

statements.text: I believe America should lead the world in AI innovation, but that progress must come with strong safeguards to protect American workers, families, and communities. [...] Given the capabilities of the latest models in aiding cyber attacks and the potential development of biological weapons, I favor regulation to ensure we protect against those threats.
statements.venue: Prince William Times candidate Q&A (emailed answers)

statements.text: That means establishing clear guardrails to protect jobs, safeguard personal data, prevent discrimination, and ensure AI is developed and deployed responsibly. It also means holding companies accountable for the enormous energy demands of data centers so Virginia families are not left footing the bill.
statements.venue: Prince William Times candidate Q&A (emailed answers)

statements.text: Data centers must pay their fair share. I regularly hear from those concerned about rising energy costs, environmental impacts, the siting of data centers and transmission lines, and the impact AI could have on their jobs.
statements.venue: Prince William Times candidate Q&A (emailed answers)

statements.text: Virginians deserve to know who is building data centers in their communities, how much energy and water these facilities consume, and whether the costs are being shifted onto them through higher utility bills. [...] My legislation will shine a light on this rapidly growing industry, hold companies accountable, and give Virginians the information they need to make informed decisions about data center development.
statements.venue: Press release on Data Center Oversight Act
